links.outcome: ML models' AUROC compared with established clinical risk scores (AUB-HAS2, RCRI) on external validation data
links.effect: No ML model showed statistically significant AUROC superiority over AUB-HAS2 (all p > 0.05), although several models modestly outperformed RCRI; Naive Bayes highest AUROC 0.738.
links.quote: However, in external validation, no ML model demonstrated statistically significant AUROC superiority over the AUB-HAS2 score (all p > 0.05), although several models modestly outperformed the RCRI.

links.outcome: Model performance when externally validated at an independent site without refitting
links.effect: Absolute risk remained underestimated in external validation; Naive Bayes had poor calibration and threshold-dependent utility; no consistent best algorithm across metrics.
links.quote: Naive Bayes achieved the highest external discrimination (AUROC 0.738, 95% CI 0.668-0.804) but showed poor calibration and threshold-dependent clinical utility.

screen.reason: The study conducts a site-separated retrospective external validation comparing multiple ML models to traditional clinical risk scores without evaluating a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
